constraints.text: Default behaviour for existing remote scopes does not change: without the new option, MOZAK still commits and pushes MOZAK.json and MOZAK.md as today.
Private plan storage never writes plan content into the linked repo's tracked files, commits, branches or remote, including on error and recovery paths.
No credentials are added: GitHub access keeps using the existing git login.

nonGoals: Hosting plan storage on a MOZAK server
Changing how local root scopes work

outcomes.criterion: With the option set, plan operations on a remote scope leave the linked repo's git history and working tree unchanged, verified by a test against a throwaway repo.
outcomes.statement: A remote scope can be configured so its plan files are stored outside the linked repo, and MOZAK never commits or pushes them there.

outcomes.criterion: mozak scopes and the Obsidian sidebar show the scope as remote, with its plans, while the plan files live in the private location.
outcomes.statement: A scope using private plan storage is still listed as a GitHub repo in mozak scopes, the MCP server and the Obsidian plugin, with its remote and ref.

outcomes.criterion: Plans, observations and receipts are identical before and after the switch; mozak check reports no issues.
outcomes.statement: An existing local scope on a clone (like obsidian-plugins-mcp today) can be switched to a remote scope with private plan storage without losing plan history.

content.purpose: Let a GitHub-linked (remote) scope keep its MOZAK.json and MOZAK.md private, so a public repo can show in MOZAK as a repo without publishing its plans.

questions.text: Where should private plan files live: a separate private git repo, a folder in the vault, or a path chosen per scope in the inventory?
What does the inventory entry look like, for example remote plus a planStore field, and how does it interact with mozak pull?
Should README.md and AGENTS.md still be read from the public repo while MOZAK.json and MOZAK.md come from the private store?

content.rationale: Remote scopes commit and push MOZAK.json and MOZAK.md into the linked repo. For a public repo that publishes plans, goals and evidence. The workaround today is a local 'root' scope on the clone, with the plan files kept out of git by hand (.git/info/exclude plus a pre-commit hook), which then shows as a plain folder, not a repo. First hit on 2026-10-14 with the public repo pitfa19/obsidian-community-plugins-mcp. Every public project will hit the same problem.

limitations: Motivating example only; its scope currently uses the local-root workaround.
Read from the installed dist build, not the source tree.

content.title: Private plan files for public GitHub scopes

constraints.text: The mozak.scope/v3 content schema does not change. Roadmap order is outcome array order. dependsOn branching is a future revision, not this plan.

Neither the renderer, the render command, nor the plugin ever writes MOZAK.json or canonical state. Projection writes go through core and stay hash-verified (bridge-stale / bridge-conflict detection keeps working).
No interactive checkboxes or clickable status anywhere in MOZAK.md. Status is symbols and mermaid only, so the owner cannot tick a box that lies.
Agents keep reading canonical state via the CLI. Nothing in this plan changes context, plans, review or decide behavior.

nonGoals: Changing the plan content schema (order or dependsOn fields).
Any write path for approvals, proposals or observations from Obsidian.
Redesigning the sidebar beyond progress strips and click-through.
Rendering pending revisions as full second roadmaps.

outcomes.criterion: The owner opens a regenerated MOZAK.md for a scope with a multi-outcome plan (e.g. ai-native-box) in Obsidian, sees the rendered roadmap and table, and accepts it as skimmable by titles and understandable in one pass.
outcomes.statement: Core's renderBridge renders each plan in MOZAK.md as a readable document: purpose, a mermaid roadmap of outcomes in array order with the current stop (first incomplete outcome) highlighted, an outcome status table (todo / evidence recorded / accepted, derived from observations, reasoning links and accept-outcome decisions), then constraints, non-goals, rationale, open questions and sources skimmable by headings. When a pending revision awaits approval, the accepted content is shown with a one-line delta summary, not a second full copy.

outcomes.criterion: Unit tests in packages/core cover each status, the current-stop inference, and that rendering a scope never changes MOZAK.json.
outcomes.statement: Outcome status in projections is derived only from canonical state: accepted when an effective accept-outcome decision exists, evidence recorded when a supporting observation with a pass verdict is linked, otherwise todo. The current stop is the first outcome in array order that is not accepted. Nothing in the projection is interactive or hand-editable.

outcomes.criterion: Running mozak render over the owner's inventory rewrites every local MOZAK.md to the new format, mozak check reports projections current, and MOZAK.json files are byte-identical before and after.
outcomes.statement: A new 'mozak render' CLI route regenerates MOZAK.md projections (one scope or all local scopes) without changing canonical state, so existing stale bridges can be refreshed after the renderer changes.

outcomes.criterion: The owner uses the rebuilt plugin in their vault: skims progress strips across scopes, clicks a plan, lands on its heading in the rendered MOZAK.md, and accepts the flow as better than the old detail tab.
outcomes.statement: The Obsidian plugin drops the PlanView detail tab. Plan rows in the sidebar show a micro progress strip (accepted outcomes / total) for open plans, and clicking a plan opens MOZAK.md at that plan's heading. The plugin may rewrite a stale MOZAK.md projection on refresh using core's renderer, but never writes MOZAK.json or any canonical state.

outcomes.criterion: The reworded guarantee appears in packages/obsidian/README.md and the rendered MOZAK.md header, and a test asserts the plugin write path can only touch MOZAK.md.
outcomes.statement: The plugin README and plugin description change from 'never writes MOZAK files' to 'never writes canonical state; may regenerate MOZAK.md projections', and the projection header still says it is generated and not to be edited.

content.purpose: Make MOZAK plans human-understandable inside Obsidian. MOZAK.md becomes the primary reading surface: per plan it renders the purpose, a display-only mermaid roadmap over the outcomes (array order, current stop = first incomplete), an outcome status table with status derived from recorded observations and owner acceptances, the full skimmable sections, and a one-line delta when a revision awaits approval. The Obsidian plugin becomes pure navigation: the PlanView detail tab is removed, plan rows gain micro progress strips, and clicking a plan jumps to its heading in MOZAK.md.

questions.text: When a scope has many plans (e.g. personal with 3+), should MOZAK.md render every plan fully, or completed plans collapsed to one line with the full rendering only for open plans?
Micro progress strip style in the sidebar: segment blocks per outcome, or a thin fill bar with a 2/5 count?

content.rationale: Decided with the owner on 2026-10-17. The owner reads plans as notes in the Obsidian editor, not in plugin panes, so the generated MOZAK.md, which today is only a plan index, is the right place for a readable rendering, and Obsidian renders mermaid in notes natively. The old PlanView mirrored schema order and read like a form; every field it showed lives in MOZAK.json and stays available via CLI, so removing it loses nothing. Settled choices: outcomes are the roadmap stops (array order), current stop is inferred as the first incomplete, full content but skimmable by titles, accepted content plus a delta line when a revision is pending, and the plugin may refresh stale projections.

limitations: Host assertion of owner messages, not native message IDs.
